detail.longDescription: I do not choose a free, paid, or self-hosted agent seat by the invoice that arrives later. I choose it by the review hours I can still spend on the diffs that seat will emit. If I cannot read the patch, the cheaper seat is not a bargain, and the expensive seat is not safer. The question I keep asking is simple: whose eyes are actually on this change before it lands? A seat is only a place where an agent edits files, runs commands, and talks back to me. The free option, the paid box, and the machine under my desk all fail in different ways when my attention runs out. I want a worksheet I can rerun on a laptop, not a slogan about which vendor feels modern this month. Would I sign the resulting commit after a tired afternoon, or would I rubber-stamp it because the queue already moved on? What this decision is, and what it is not I am deciding where a bounded agent task may run, and what evidence must come back with it. I am not deciding which model is smartest, because I have not measured that on this repository. I am not deciding a permanent architecture, because availability, quotas, and hardware change without asking me. Can I name the files the agent may touch, and can I name the files it must never open? Three seats stay on the table until the sheet says otherwise, and I do not drop one early. A free hosted seat means free model access plus a free server option, when those are currently offered, and nothing more specific. A paid hosted seat means I am buying priority, retention, or a support path I can name in a contract. A self-hosted seat means I already own the runner, the logs, and the failure, including the night it falls over. Disclosure: This article was prepared as part of MonkeyCode's product outreach. I mention MonkeyCode here because its free model access and free server option are one concrete way to fill the free hosted column. I do not treat that mention as a measurement of quality, uptime, token allowance, or model identity. If a quota, a model name, or a hardware shape matters to you, read the current docs before you plan a sprint around them. Fit criteria I refuse to skip I score each seat against the questions below, and I write the answers in plain text next to the task. What data class sits in the workspace: a public fixture, internal code without secrets, or anything regulated? How many review minutes can I honestly give this task before the week ends and the context fades? Can I export the diff, the test log, and the prompt, and who reruns the job if the seat vanishes? A free hosted seat fits a public fixture or a synthetic bug, when losing the session would only cost a rerun. It does not fit when secrets, customer data, or a release branch sit in the same tree as the task. A paid hosted seat fits when I need a named retention window or a support contact, and when review time is already funded. A self-hosted seat fits when the data cannot leave, and when I can actually patch the runner myself. Would I still pick the free seat if the docs changed the allowance tomorrow morning without notice? Only if the task is disposable and the evidence already lives on my disk, where a vanished tab cannot take it. Would I pick self-hosted for a one-file typo in a public sample that nobody is waiting on? Probably not, because I would spend the afternoon nursing a runner instead of reading the diff itself. A local gate you can reread The script below is a proposal, not a benchmark I have executed against a live vendor. It reads a small JSON description of the task and prints which seats remain eligible today. You can change the thresholds, but do not pretend those numbers came from a measured lab. I keep the inputs boring on purpose, so a teammate can argue with a field instead of arguing with a vibe. # !/usr/bin/env python3 """Proposal only: gate agent seats by data class and review budget. Unexecuted example. It does not call a vendor API and it does not measure model quality. Replace the sample task before you trust it. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import sys from dataclasses import dataclass @dataclass(frozen=True) class Task: data_class: str # public_fixture | internal_code | regulated review_minutes: int expected_diff_lines: int needs_named_support: bool can_export_locally: bool secrets_in_tree: bool def eligible(task: Task) -> dict[str, str]: reasons: dict[str, str] = {} leaves_blocked = task.secrets_in_tree or task.data_class == "regulated" if leaves_blocked: reasons["free_hosted"] = "blocked: data must not leave the machine" reasons["paid_hosted"] = "blocked: data must not leave the machine" elif task.data_class == "public_fixture" and task.can_export_locally: reasons["free_hosted"] = "eligible: disposable work and local evidence" elif task.data_class == "internal_code" and task.can_export_locally: reasons["free_hosted"] = "hold: confirm current data terms before use" else: reasons["free_hosted"] = "blocked: no local export path" if not leaves_blocked and (task.needs_named_support or task.review_minutes >= 90): reasons["paid_hosted"] = "eligible: support or a funded review window" elif not leaves_blocked: reasons["paid_hosted"] = "optional: only if the contract names retention" if leaves_blocked or task.data_class == "internal_code": reasons["self_hosted"] = "eligible: you keep the runner and the logs" elif task.expected_diff_lines <= 80 and task.review_minutes <= 45: reasons["self_hosted"] = "skip: runner care exceeds the diff" else: reasons["self_hosted"] = "optional: use if you already operate the box" return reasons def main() -> int: raw = json.load(sys.stdin) task = Task( data_class=raw["data_class"], review_minutes=int(raw["review_minutes"]), expected_diff_lines=int(raw["expected_diff_lines"]), needs_named_support=bool(raw["needs_named_support"]), can_export_locally=bool(raw["can_export_locally"]), secrets_in_tree=bool(raw["secrets_in_tree"]), ) print(json.dumps(eligible(task), indent=2)) return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main()) The command below only runs that local script, and it does not call a remote agent or upload the fixture. Swap the JSON for your own notes, and keep secrets out of the file even on your laptop. If you cannot describe the task without pasting a credential, stop and shrink the workspace first. A worksheet that requires a secret in order to run is already telling you the free hosted column is closed. python3 seat_gate.py <<'JSON' { "data_class": "public_fixture", "review_minutes": 40, "expected_diff_lines": 60, "needs_named_support": false, "can_export_locally": true, "secrets_in_tree": false } JSON I feed it a fixture that looks like the work, not like a marketing page I saw this week. A public parser bug with a short guess and half an hour of review should not drag a regulated workspace into the same decision. If the printout says hold, I stop and read the terms, because a script cannot grant a permission that policy never gave. Would I be comfortable pasting that JSON into the ticket where my reviewer can see every field? Steps I follow before I trust a column I copy the task into a scratch repository that contains no secrets, no customer dumps, and no production environment files. If I cannot make that copy, the free hosted column is already closed, and I do not negotiate with myself. A missing fixture is a data decision, not a tooling inconvenience I can wave away later. I write the expected diff size in lines, then I reserve review minutes at about one minute per five changed lines. I add fifteen minutes to read the test log, and I raise that guess when the patch touches concurrency or authentication. That ratio is a personal planning habit, not a measured law you should quote as science. I run the worksheet and I keep every hold or blocked line in the pull request description. A green eligible mark is permission to try a seat, not permission to merge the result. Would I still merge if the reviewer asked me to explain the prompt from memory alone? I capture evidence on my own disk before I close the session: the diff, the command, and the short prompt. A free server option is useful only when that capture still works after the browser tab dies. I use a local archive so the seat cannot become the only copy of the reasoning. mkdir -p handoff && git diff > handoff/agent.diff # Replace the echo with the real prompt. Do not paste secrets. { echo "prompt: reproduce the public fixture only"; git status --short; } > handoff/notes.txt sha256sum handoff/agent.diff handoff/notes.txt > handoff/SHA256SUMS I compare the three columns only after that archive already exists on my own laptop disk. Free hosted stays in the running when the fixture is public and the archive is complete. Paid hosted stays when I need a support path or a retention promise I can point to in writing. Self-hosted stays when the data class forbids leaving, and when I can operate the box without stealing review time. I rerun the same fixture once on the seat I picked, and once locally from the saved diff, before I talk about speed. If the local rerun fails, the seat did not save me time, because I still cannot explain the change. How many of last week's agent patches could I still rebuild from the notes I actually kept? Tradeoffs I want written down I keep a short table so the argument does not collapse into a price screenshot from a vendor page. The cells are fit notes, not scores I measured on identical hardware during some quiet week. I will not fill those cells with token counts, GPU names, or uptime percentages I cannot re-check next week. A number I cannot point to in a current primary document is not a decision input for this sheet. QuestionFree hostedPaid hostedSelf-hostedMay the workspace leave your network?Treat as yes until current terms say otherwiseTreat as yes unless the contract says otherwiseNo, if the runner stays inside your boundaryWhat you might be paying withReview time, plus a rerun if the session diesMoney, contract reading, and the same review timeReview time plus runner maintenanceWhat a bad day looks likeAllowance or session changes under youThe bill grows while your review hours stay fixedBox care steals the afternoon you reservedWhat you must already holdA local archive of diff, command, and promptThat archive, plus the clause you relied onThat archive, plus notes a teammate can boot If MonkeyCode's free model access or free server option is the free hosted candidate, confirm the live limits before you start. Write those limits into the ticket yourself, with the date you read them, so next week's reader is not guessing. I am not claiming a token grant, a duration, or a hardware shape, because no primary source for those figures was attached here. Would you trust a sprint plan that depended on a number nobody could open in a browser today? Who should walk away This sheet does not tell you which model writes better patches, and it will not catch a subtle bug because the fixture was public. It assumes you can make a secret-free copy, which is false for plenty of real services that mix config into the tree. It also assumes a human still merges, which is false if your pipeline applies agent output without a reviewer in the loop. Do not use this approach for production credentials, regulated records, or any path where an agent can push alone. Do not use a free hosted seat as a silent default for the whole monorepo just because that column looked cheap. Do not use self-hosted as a moral upgrade if nobody on the team can restore the runner after a bad image. Do not use a paid seat to skip the archive step, because a receipt is not a diff you can explain later. I would rather throw away a free exploration than explain a missing prompt three days after the session died. If the worksheet marks a public fixture as eligible for a free hosted seat, that is when I open the current MonkeyCode docs. I check whether free model access and the free server option still match the task I wrote down. I keep the same fixture, the same archive commands, and the same refusal rules if I later move that task. The seat can change next week, but the evidence I am willing to merge should not change with the invoice. # ai # devops # tutorial # productivity # software # coding # development # engineering # inclusive # community A Review-Hour Gate for Free, Paid, and Local Agent Work
